course_name_original: Practică pentru elaborarea proiectului de diplomă
course_name_en: Practice for the development of the degree project

learning_outcomes.text: Knows the operating principles of automotive propulsion systems, performance requirements, and safety.
Understands testing, diagnostic, and validation procedures applicable in the automotive industry.
Knows the use of CAD/CAE software and measurement and control equipment.
Understands occupational safety regulations and applicable quality standards.
Performs diagnostic and verification operations on thermal, hybrid, and electric propulsion systems.
Uses modern equipment and specific software for simulation and validation.
Prepares technical documentation related to practical activities.
Applies standardized procedures to ensure quality and conformity.
Plans and manages practical activities autonomously, respecting deadlines and quality requirements.
Respects safety regulations and academic integrity.
Collaborates efficiently in multidisciplinary teams and communicates technically clearly.
Self-evaluates progress and adopts measures for improving results.

syllabus_topics: Occupational safety, general instructions, specific instructions for the practice location, fire safety instructions
Preparation of the organizational sketch of the place where the practical activity takes place. Presentation of the company.
Description of technological processes in the sectors where the practical activity takes place.
Constructive-functional analysis of technological lines, mechanical transmissions in road vehicle construction, thermal equipment, mechatronics, and robots. Preparation of kinematic diagrams
Knowledge of the main types of mechanical processing
General aspects regarding the use of computer programs in the design of mechanical and mechatronic systems within the company or firm
teaching_methods: Applied demonstrations on propulsion systems and dedicated stands
Use of CAD/CAE software and diagnostic equipment
assessment_rules: The competencies acquired during the practice period are presented in a practice report prepared by the student according to the analytical program. The report is presented orally through direct communication with the practice supervisor. The final evaluation result is based on the scores and weights allocated to each activity. Grades from 1 to 10 will be awarded, with a grade of 5 certifying the achievement of minimal learning outcomes and the granting of corresponding study credits.
